message: Reviewed from dated primary evidence using the Codex subscription.

data.headline: IWM: cheaper overnight money is not a cheaper small-business loan.
data.summary: The overnight secured rate fell on November 4, while the two-year Treasury yield had risen the day before. For a small company facing refinancing, a lender’s spread and terms can matter more than either benchmark.

bull.text: SOFR slipped from 3.97% to 3.94% between November 3 and 4. A borrower whose rate resets against SOFR could see a lower benchmark component; its spread and reset date would still matter.

bear.text: The two-year Treasury yield rose from 4.59% to 4.61% on November 3. A company refinancing for a longer term therefore faced a different benchmark backdrop from the one suggested by overnight funding.

watch.text: Russell 2000 futures asset managers were net long 19,602 contracts and leveraged funds net short 48,081 on October 27. Neither balance is a count of loans, defaults or flows into IWM.

limitations: The evidence does not include small-company loan spreads, actual loan resets, IWM prices or credit losses. The October futures report predates November’s funding readings.
The available evidence does not support a calibrated forecast or a directional trading call.

sources.title: CFTC · RUSSELL E-MINI - CHICAGO MERCANTILE EXCHANGE · 2026-10-27
